artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Charles Kim appealed discipline imposed by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission that had replaced the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to the Session, not the presbytery commission, reversed the presbytery's action and censure, and held that the commission's acts were unauthorized without congregational consent.

artifacts.title: Appeal Deacon Samuel Hong v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 142
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's censure of Deacon Samuel Hong, finding that the Presbytery lacked original jurisdiction over communicant members and should have been tried in the Session. The court held that regardless of the merits of the underlying charges (contumacy and making false statements), the procedural violation of jurisdiction was fatal to the action.

artifacts.title: Appeal RE Choon Soon Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 149
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's action in adjudicating charges against RE Choon Soon Lee. The court held that a ruling elder member of a local congregation may only be subject to judicial process originating in the Session of that church, not in the Presbytery, as the Session has original jurisdiction over its members.

artifacts.title: Appeal RE Joo Bok Suh v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 147
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by RE Joo Bok Suh challenging the Korean Capital Presbytery's attempt to exercise original jurisdiction over charges of making false statements on official documents related to church trustee replacement. The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the presbytery's action, holding that original jurisdiction over communicant members must reside with the Session of the church to which they belong, not with the Presbytery.

artifacts.title: Complaint TE Larry Ball v. Westminster Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 162
artifacts.synopsis: TE Larry Ball complained that Westminster Presbytery erred in approving a plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC affirmed that a presbytery has the constitutional right to withdraw from the PCA as part of historic American grass-roots Presbyterianism, subject to proper procedures. The court held that the relationship between General Assembly and presbytery mirrors that between presbytery and local church, protecting each level's distinct identity and civil operations.
